name: Queen Anne

about.summary: The style many think of as Victorian: towers, porches, bays and patterned walls, no two sides alike.

cues.explain: A round or many-sided tower, often at a corner of the house.
A wide porch across part or all of the front.
Gables, bays and towers jut out, so the front is never symmetrical.
Patterned shingles, brick and half-timbering can all appear on one house.

plate_gap: No cleared plate yet. Prairie Avenue had Queen Anne houses, but no source read names one, and the public-domain views in the image library are of houses whose style no source states. A plate needs a public-domain image of a building a source calls Queen Anne.
